label: <DEL> step of long sequences starting with z/s/p/l/1/a/k/q/b/n
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (93% of activation mass; 11.6% of <DEL> steps are active), i.e. the step where the model outputs original token 0. Which <DEL> steps fire depends on (a) the first original token, which is also the token being output: z, s, p, l, 1, a, k, q, b, n give the highest rates (z highest at about 6%) and w, f the lowest; and (b) sequence length, with the rate rising steeply as L goes up (L=9 is most active). The strongest activations are at <DEL> in L=8-9 sequences. There is weak, small firing on late original-phase steps (t>=4, mostly on inputs e, t, u, about 6% of mass) and essentially none in the copy phase or on the first 3 steps. The first-token and length conditions only partly sort the <DEL> steps: many qualifying sequences stay below threshold, so precision is low (about 0.39) and what decides the rest is unexplained (it is not the presence of e/t/u).
